questions.q: Find the personal liability of the sole proprietor. Use the method 'Sole Proprietorship and Personal Liability'. Work with: business_assets = 12000, deficit = 240, total_liabilities = 5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 240 rupees

questions.q: Calculate the amount the owner must contribute from personal assets to clear debts. Use the method 'Sole Proprietorship and Personal Liability'. Work with: business_assets = 1200, deficit = 3, total_liabilities = 300. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 3 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sole Proprietorship and Personal Liability' refers to.
questions.a: A commercial setup owned, managed, and controlled entirely by a single person who bears full risk and reaps all rewards.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sole Proprietorship and Personal Liability'.
questions.a: The sole owner carries unlimited liability, meaning personal assets can be liquidated if business assets fall short of debts.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Sole Proprietorship and Personal Liability', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: personal_liability = max(0, total_liabilities - business_assets)

concepts.title: Joint Hindu Family Business Structure and Governance

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Joint Hindu Family Business Structure and Governance' refers to.
questions.a: A unique traditional Indian business enterprise owned jointly by coparceners of an undivided Hindu family and administered by the eldest member.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Joint Hindu Family Business Structure and Governance'.
questions.a: Membership is acquired by birth; coparceners enjoy limited liability whereas the Karta bears unlimited personal liability.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Joint Hindu Family Business Structure and Governance', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: coparcener_liability = capital_share, karta_liability = unlimited

questions.q: Using the method 'Partnership Essentials and Mutual Agency', work with: partner_ratio = 80, total_profit = 80000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of profit_share.
questions.a: 6400000 rupees

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Partnership Essentials and Mutual Agency' and work with: partner_ratio = 5, total_profit = 20000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of profit_share.
questions.a: 100000 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Partnership Essentials and Mutual Agency' refers to.
questions.a: An association of two or more individuals who have agreed to pool resources to operate a lawful business and distribute profits and losses.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Partnership Essentials and Mutual Agency'.
questions.a: Every partner acts simultaneously as an agent capable of binding others and as a principal bound by the acts of co-partners.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Partnership Essentials and Mutual Agency', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: profit_share = total_profit * partner_ratio

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Classification and Liabilities of Partners' refers to.
questions.a: The categorization of partners based on capital contribution, operational management, profit sharing, and exposure to liability.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Classification and Liabilities of Partners'.
questions.a: Partners by estoppel, holding out, and nominal partners do not contribute capital or manage, yet carry unlimited liability to third parties.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Classification and Liabilities of Partners', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: liability_status = unlimited (except admitted minors)

questions.q: Using the method 'Consequences of Non-Registration of Partnership', work with: suit_against_copartners = 5, suit_against_third_party = 3. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of legal_disability.
questions.a: 8 rupees

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Consequences of Non-Registration of Partnership' and work with: suit_against_copartners = 24, suit_against_third_party = 20. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of legal_disability.
questions.a: 44 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Consequences of Non-Registration of Partnership' refers to.
questions.a: The legal disabilities imposed on an unregistered partnership firm under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Consequences of Non-Registration of Partnership'.
questions.a: Although registration is optional, non-registered firms lose the right to enforce contractual claims in a court of law against partners or external parties.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Consequences of Non-Registration of Partnership', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: legal_disability = suit_against_third_party + suit_against_copartners

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Cooperative Society Principles and Characteristics' refers to.
questions.a: A voluntary organization established by individuals of limited financial resources to promote mutual economic welfare based on self-help and democratic governance.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cooperative Society Principles and Characteristics'.
questions.a: Democratic control operates on the rule of 'one man, one vote' irrespective of the capital contributed by an individual member.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Cooperative Society Principles and Characteristics', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: voting_power = 1_member_1_vote

questions.q: Using the method 'Types of Cooperative Societies', work with: based_on_patronage_or_capital = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of surplus_distribution.
questions.a: 100 rupees

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Types of Cooperative Societies' and work with: based_on_patronage_or_capital = 1000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of surplus_distribution.
questions.a: 1000 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Types of Cooperative Societies' refers to.
questions.a: Classification of cooperative societies based on their specific functional objectives such as consumer protection, producer aid, marketing, farming, credit, or housing.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Types of Cooperative Societies'.
questions.a: Different cooperative types target distinct economic challenges of specific groups like small farmers, artisans, borrowers, or consumers.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Types of Cooperative Societies', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: surplus_distribution = based_on_patronage_or_capital

concepts.title: Joint Stock Company and Shareholder Liability

questions.q: Calculate the maximum liability of a shareholder in a joint stock company. Use the method 'Joint Stock Company and Shareholder Liability'. Work with: face_value = 500, num_shares = 40, paid_amount = 20000, unpaid_per_share = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 4000 rupees

questions.q: Find the remaining financial obligation of a shareholder on partly paid shares. Use the method 'Joint Stock Company and Shareholder Liability'. Work with: face_value = 80000, num_shares = 100, paid_amount = 12000, unpaid_per_share = 5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
questions.a: 500 rupees

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Joint Stock Company and Shareholder Liability' refers to.
questions.a: An incorporated artificial legal entity with perpetual succession, a separate legal personality, and capital divisible into transferable shares.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Joint Stock Company and Shareholder Liability'.
questions.a: A shareholder's liability is strictly limited to the unpaid portion of the nominal value of the shares held.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Joint Stock Company and Shareholder Liability', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: unpaid_liability = num_shares * (face_value - paid_amount)

concepts.title: Distinction Between Private and Public Companies

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Distinction Between Private and Public Companies' refers to.
questions.a: The statutory differentiation of corporate entities under the Companies Act based on share transferability, public invitations, and membership thresholds.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Distinction Between Private and Public Companies'.
questions.a: A private company restricts share transfers and public subscriptions with a 200-member ceiling, whereas a public company has free share transferability and no maximum member limit.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Distinction Between Private and Public Companies', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: public_min_members = 7, private_min_members = 2

concepts.title: Factors Determining Choice of Business Organisation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Factors Determining Choice of Business Organisation' refers to.
questions.a: The strategic evaluation of organizational forms across capital needs, liability tolerance, regulatory compliance, managerial complexity, and operational continuity.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Factors Determining Choice of Business Organisation'.
questions.a: Higher capital and expansion requirements favor corporate forms, while personal customer touch, quick decisions, and minimal capital favor sole proprietorship.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Factors Determining Choice of Business Organisation', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: choice_suitability = f(capital, liability, continuity, management, control)
